test2_whitehead_borromean_ratio.note: 7.2% near-miss; Catalan-multiple coincidence; conflicts with Hopf registry

data.verdict: REFUTED. (b) The LITERAL option #1 (w_n = hyperbolic volume of the n-body sub-link of the Borromean atom 𝓑_K) is STRUCTURALLY EXCLUDED at n=2: the 2-body sub-link is non-hyperbolic (Vol=0) — the Borromean rings are Brunnian, so removing any one component leaves the 2-component unlink, and the SDP binding-link registry independently assigns the deuteron bond to the Hopf link (Seifert-fibred, Vol=0). Either way the n=2 volume vanishes, but the extracted w_2 = 4.353 > 0. Cited invariant: Brunnian / Seifert-fibred non-hyperbolicity (Vol=0). (a) Re-choosing the links (Whitehead for n=2, Borromean for n=3) gives the parameter-free 1:2 Catalan ratio vs observed w_3/w_2 = 2.143 — a 7.2% NEAR-MISS, not a closure, AND it contradicts the registry's Hopf assignment for the deuteron bond, so the match is a numerical coincidence of Catalan multiples, not a derivation. Net: the volume route does not supply w_n. Consistent with the companion probe (w_n is the gated W_λ multiplier, sub-geometric); the na-Stokes kernel a_D^(n) stays permanent. No production touch; no value wired; no tier change.
